**Note to Users**: The primary requirement to run the Blue Water Potential Toolkit (`02_blue-water.qmd`) is the set of standardized CSV outputs produced by this script. 

### 🗂️ Workflow & Data Summary

This script processes, standardizes, and expands seven distinct categories of input data required by the hydrological model for a given agrarian system:

1. **Climatic Forcings**: Multi-year Daily Precipitation and Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0).
2. **Soil Properties**: Water Holding Capacity (WHC) and Readily Available Water (RAW).
3. **Crop Parameters**: Rooting depths and whether the crop is irrigated or rainfed.
4. **Crop Cycle**: Sowing date, Crop phenological phase duration and respective crop coefficients (Kc) according to FAO56 method (Allen et al., 1998).
5. **Cropping Systems**: Crop rotation at the plot scale.
6. **Farm production systems**: Agregation of grazed and cropped area (ha) for each farming system.
7. **Agrarian system**: Area (ha) of each farm production system (ha) in a given village/micro-region.

In Hemingway et al. (202X), this process was run for two agrarian systems, corresponding to two historical periods, 1950s and 2022. The climate time series (1980-2018) was the same for the two periods analysed, while cropping systems, productions systems and agrarian systems were period-specific.

### 📂 Directory Structure for this Script

This script serves two purposes: it can be used to reproduce the results presented in the manuscript Hemingway et al. (202X), and it can be used to apply the method in your specific study sites.

* **Reproducing the Manuscript:** All clean inputs required to run this script are provided in the `data/input/` directory.
* **Adapting for your own study site:** Place your clean data in the correct starting locations shown below. The script will automatically generate the required folder structure for all derived processed outputs if they do not exist. To run this script, open the `.Rproj` and click "Render".

```text
project_root/
├── data/
│   ├── input/               <- REQUIRED: Place your standardized CSVs here
│   │   ├── 01_precipitation.csv
│   │   ├── 02_et0.csv
│   │   ├── 03_soil.parameters.csv
│   │   ├── 04_crop.parameters.csv
│   │   ├── 05_crop_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv
│   │   ├── 06_fruit_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv (optional)
│   │   ├── 07_crop.systems.csv
│   │   ├── 08_crop_system_area_by_production_system.csv
│   │   └── 09_no_of_production_system_in_the_agrarian_system.csv
│       └── supplementary/01_monthly_climatology_for_figure.csv (optional)
│   └── processed/           <- Generated: Derived model requirements (e.g., Kc curves) will land here
│       └── supplementary/   <- Generated: Intermediary Kc tables will land here
├── code/
│   ├── functions/
│   ├── 01_Prepare_Model_Inputs.qmd  <- (This file)
│   └── 01_Prepare_Model_Inputs.html <- Generated: HTML Report created by rendering this script
└── Blue-Water.Rproj         <- Required: RStudio Project file to render this script

```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls(all.names = TRUE)); gc()

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, here, knitr, rmarkdown)

# Ensure output directories exist
new.dirs <- list(here("data/processed"), here("data/processed/supplementary"))
lapply(new.dirs, function(x) if (!dir.exists(x)) dir.create(x, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE))

# Source core biophysical dependencies globally
source(here("code/functions/01_get_kc.R"))
source(here("code/functions/03_expand_kc.R"))

# =====================================================================
# GRASSLAND GROWTH CYCLE PARAMETERS
# =====================================================================
biophysical_parameters <- list(
  grazing_growth_rate   = 0.00458333333333333,
  grazing_drop_kc       = 0.20,
  grazing_max_kc        = 0.75,
  napier_decline_rate_1 = 0.000307692307692308,
  napier_decline_rate_2 = 0.000153846153846154
)

theme_baseR <- theme_bw() + theme(
  panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black"), 
  strip.background = element_blank()
)

# Climatic Data (Forcing Variables)

The water balance model requires continuous, daily forcing variables. Here, we read the required daily Precipitation (P) and Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0).

```{r clim-load}
precip <- data.table::fread(here("data/input/01_precipitation.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
et0.daily <- data.table::fread(here("data/input/02_et0.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
et0.daily <- et0.daily %>%
  mutate(et0 = round(et0, 3))
stopifnot(
  "Error: Precipitation contains missing values (NA)." = !any(is.na(precip$p)),
  "Error: ET0 contains missing values (NA)." = !any(is.na(et0.daily$et0))
)
# Only for figure plotting
climate_summary <- data.table::fread(here("data/input/supplementary/01_monthly_climatology_for_figure.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
```

#### Precipitation

```{r precip-display, echo=FALSE}
preview_precip <- head(precip, 5)

)
knitr::kable(preview_precip, escape = FALSE, caption = "Preview: Precipitation Data Sample")

write.csv(precip, file = here("data/processed/01_precipitation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## Crop Coefficient (Kc) Curves

Our framework dynamically generates daily Kc curves over a calendar year from the input parameters. As described in the manuscript, daily Kc values are computed based on the FAO method for most crops, monthly step functions for some fruit trees, or polynomial equations for groundnut, or linear regrowth rules for grasslands. Some crops such as banana can span multiple years, in which case we define a crop coefficient curve of each year independently.

```{r load-kc-params}
fao_kc_raw       <- data.table::fread(here("data/input/05_crop_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
fruit_kc_raw   <- data.table::fread(here("data/input/06_fruit_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
```

#### FAO Segmented Parameters

```{r fao-params-display, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(fao_kc_raw, 5), caption = "Preview: FAO Segmented Parameters")

```

#### Fruit Tree Parameters

```{r fruit-params-display, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(fruit_kc_raw, caption = "Preview: Fruit Tree Parameters")

```

---

We pass the input Kc parameters through mathematical functions. This includes standard FAO-56 segmented curves for standard crops, derived 4th-order polynomial equations for continuous rapid growth crops like Groundnuts, and complex daily linear regrowth rates for pastures and harvested grasses.

### Standard FAO-56 Segmented Curves

Generates the classic 4-stage linear growth curves for standard crops.

```{r generate-fao-kc, warning=FALSE, fig.cap="Standard FAO-56 segmented curves based on major crop calendar events such as sowing and harvesting dates, and crop development duration."}
fao_kc_raw.long <- fao_kc_raw %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -1, names_to = "crop") %>% 
  mutate(crop = str_to_title(gsub("_|\\.", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)))

kc <- fao_kc_raw.long %>% subset(stringr::str_detect(var, stringr::regex("kc", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% rename(Kc = value, kc_var = var) %>%
  mutate(Kc_var = case_when(grepl("ini", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_ini", grepl("mid", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_mid", grepl("end", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_end", TRUE ~ kc_var))

doy <- fao_kc_raw.long %>% subset(var %in% c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest")) %>% rename(doy = value, doy_var = var) %>% mutate(doy = if_else(doy == 365.00, 366.00, doy))

kc.doy.key <- data.frame(doy_var = c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest"), kc_var = c("Kc_ini", "Kc_ini", "Kc_mid", "Kc_mid", "Kc_end"))

doy <- left_join(doy, kc.doy.key, by = c("doy_var"))
kc.doy <- left_join(doy, kc, by = c("kc_var", "crop")) %>% arrange(crop, doy, Kc) %>% mutate(doy = as.numeric(doy), Kc = as.numeric(Kc))

kc.doy.crops <- kc.doy %>% select(crop, doy_var, doy, Kc) %>%
  mutate(doy_var = factor(doy_var, levels = c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest"))) %>%
  arrange(crop, doy, doy_var)

kc_wide_build <- kc.doy.crops %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = doy_var, values_from = c(doy, Kc)) %>%
  rename(
    Sow = doy_Sowing, E_ini = `doy_End of ini`, E_dev = `doy_End of Dev`,
    E_mid = `doy_End of Mid`, Harv = doy_Harvest,
    K_ini = Kc_Sowing, K_mid = `Kc_End of Dev`, K_end = Kc_Harvest
  )

kc_segmented_ls <- lapply(1:nrow(kc_wide_build), function(i) build_fao_curve(kc_wide_build[i, ]))
kc_segmented <- bind_rows(kc_segmented_ls) %>%
  mutate(crop = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)))

# Visual Check
ggplot(kc_segmented %>% mutate(plot_kc = if_else(kc == 0, NA_real_, kc)), aes(x = doy, y = plot_kc, color = crop)) +
  # NEW: Add a subtle color fill beneath the curve. This makes active panels stand out.
  geom_area(ggplot2::aes(fill = crop), alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) + facet_wrap(~ crop) + theme_baseR +
  labs(title = "Standard FAO-56 Curves", x = "Day of Year", y = "Kc") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Polynomial Curves

Applies 4th-order polynomial equations to capture continuous rapid growth dynamics (e.g., Groundnuts).

```{r generate-poly-kc, warning=FALSE, out.width="70%", fig.cap="Continuous polynomial curves modeling the rapid growth dynamics of groundnuts."}
gs <- data.frame(doy = 1:366) %>%
  mutate(crop = "Groundnut Summer", d = doy - 10, kc = if_else(d >= 0 & d <= 104, 1.25*10^(-7)*d^4 - 2.82*10^(-5)*d^3 + 1.8*10^(-3)*d^2 - 2.49*10^(-2)*d + 0.3792, 0))

gm <- data.frame(doy = 1:366) %>%
  mutate(crop = "Groundnut Monsoon", d = doy - 182, kc = if_else(d >= 0 & d <= 104, 1.32*10^(-7)*d^4 - 2.99*10^(-5)*d^3 + 1.96*10^(-3)*d^2 - 3.02*10^(-2)*d + 0.4, 0))

kc_polynomial <- bind_rows(gm, gs) %>% select(-d)

# Visual Check
ggplot(kc_polynomial %>% mutate(plot_kc = if_else(kc == 0, NA_real_, kc)), 
       aes(x = doy, y = plot_kc, color = crop)) +
  geom_area(ggplot2::aes(fill = crop), alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) + 
  facet_wrap(. ~ crop, ncol = 1) + theme_baseR +
  labs(x = "Day of Year", y = "Kc") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )

```

kc_fruits <- bind_rows(generate_fruit_step("Pomegranate", fruit_kc_raw), generate_fruit_step("Sweet Lime", fruit_kc_raw))

    legend.position = "none",

    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )

```

### Grasslands and Fodder Crops

Applies calibrated drop-and-regrowth rates for grazed pastures and harvested Napier grass.

```{r kc-complex, warning=FALSE, fig.cap="Complex harvesting and regrowth schedules illustrating calibrated drop-and-regrowth rates for grazed pastures and Napier grass."}
no_crop <- tibble(doy = 1:366, crop = "No Crop", kc = 0)
grassland_base <- kc_segmented %>% filter(crop == "Grasslands") %>% pull(kc)

growth_rate  <- biophysical_parameters$grazing_growth_rate
napier_dec_1 <- biophysical_parameters$napier_decline_rate_1
napier_dec_2 <- biophysical_parameters$napier_decline_rate_2
graze_drop   <- biophysical_parameters$grazing_drop_kc 
max_bound    <- biophysical_parameters$grazing_max_kc  
grassland_sow <- kc_wide_build$Sow[kc_wide_build$crop == "Grasslands"]

grazed_thrice <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed Thrice", c(182, 243, 304), grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_aug  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Aug", 213, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_sept <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Sept", 244, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_oct  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Oct", 274, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_nov  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Nov", 306, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)

napier       <- generate_napier("Napier", 1, napier_dec_1, napier_dec_2)
napier_short <- generate_napier("Napier Short", 211, napier_dec_1, napier_dec_2)

# Visual Check
complex_plot_data <- bind_rows(grazed_thrice, grazed_1_aug, grazed_1_sept, grazed_1_oct, grazed_1_nov, napier, napier_short)

ggplot(complex_plot_data %>% mutate(plot_kc = if_else(kc == 0, NA_real_, kc)), aes(x = doy, y = plot_kc, color = crop)) +
  geom_area(ggplot2::aes(fill = crop), alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) + facet_wrap(~ crop) + theme_baseR +
  labs(title = "Complex Harvesting & Regrowth Curves", x = "Day of Year", y = "Kc") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

#### Kc Curve compilation for all crops

Compile all generated Kc curves.

```{r kc-merge}
kc.doy.crop.all <- bind_rows(
  kc_segmented, kc_polynomial, kc_fruits, no_crop,
  grazed_thrice, grazed_1_aug, grazed_1_sept, grazed_1_oct, grazed_1_nov, 
  napier, napier_short
) %>% arrange(crop, doy)

write.csv(kc.doy.crop.all, file = here("data/processed/supplementary/02_crop_kc_by_doy_all_crops.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```


# Cropping Systems

Read the file that describes the composition of each cropping system in terms of crop rotations at the plot scale.

```{r, load-cropping-systems}
crop.systems <- data.table::fread(here("data/input/07_crop.systems.csv")) %>% as_tibble()

write.csv(crop.systems, file = here("data/processed/05_crop.systems.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(head(crop.systems), caption = "Preview: Cropping Systems")

# Generate the long-format rotation table
crop.systems.l <- crop.systems %>%
  select(-Irrigation) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("crop_"), names_prefix = "crop_", names_to = "ncrop", values_to = "crop") %>%
  left_join(crop.param, by = "crop")
```

## Build annual/multi-annual cropping systems/rotations by compiling individual Crop Kc Curves.

```{r map-kc-curves, results='hide'}
crop.systems.l.kc <- crop.systems.l %>%
  select(rotation, n.rotation, crop.system, soil, ncrop, crop, irrigation, rooting_depth_cm) %>%
  left_join(kc.doy.crop.all %>% arrange(doy, crop), by = "crop", relationship = "many-to-many")
```

### Daily Kc Table by Crop Rotation

# Agrarian System

Read the file with number of farms belonging to each of the Production Systems in the Agrarian System of the considered area (village, micro-region, watershed). In our case study these numbers are calculated for two periods using an optimisation technique as described in Hemingway et al. 2026.

```{r load-agrirarian}
farms_count_df <- data.table::fread(here("data/input/09_no_of_farmers_by_production_system.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
```

# References
